claim: Fibrolamellar carcinoma (FLC) is a rare liver cancer.
source: Fibrolamellar carcinoma (FLC) is a rare liver cancer.
evidence: This is a definitional statement presented in the abstract and introduction of the manuscript.

claim: FLCs uniquely produce DNAJ-PKAc, a chimeric enzyme consisting of a chaperonin-binding domain fused to the Cα subunit of protein kinase A.
source: FLCs uniquely produce DNAJ-PKAc, a chimeric enzyme consisting of a chaperonin-binding domain fused to the Cα subunit of protein kinase A.
evidence: This statement is supported by the manuscript's biochemical analyses and is consistent with cited literature on FLC.

claim: A unique property of the DNAJ-PKAc fusion enzyme is the ability to recruit heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70).
source: Biochemical analyses of clinical samples reveal that a unique property of this fusion enzyme is the ability to recruit heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 1H and proximity ligation assays in Figure 1I-K.

claim: Heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70) is frequently up-regulated in cancers.
source: This cellular chaperonin is frequently up-regulated in cancers.
evidence: This statement references established scientific knowledge about Hsp70 in cancer, supported by citations in the manuscript (Calderwood et al., 2006; Mayer and Bukau, 2005).

claim: Gene-editing of mouse hepatocytes generated disease-relevant AML12DNAJ-PKAc cell lines.
source: Gene-editing of mouse hepatocytes generated disease-relevant AML12DNAJ-PKAc cell lines.
evidence: This is supported by the detailed CRISPR/Cas9 methodology and characterization data presented in Figure 2.

claim: The proto-oncogene A-kinase anchoring protein-Lbc is up-regulated in FLC.
source: Further analyses indicate that the proto-oncogene A-kinase anchoring protein-Lbc is up-regulated in FLC and functions to cluster DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 sub-complexes with a RAF-MEK-ERK kinase module.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data in Figure 5B showing elevated AKAP-Lbc protein levels in FLC compared to normal adjacent liver.

claim: AKAP-Lbc functions to cluster DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 sub-complexes with a RAF-MEK-ERK kinase module.
source: Further analyses indicate that the proto-oncogene A-kinase anchoring protein-Lbc is up-regulated in FLC and functions to cluster DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 sub-complexes with a RAF-MEK-ERK kinase module.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments in Figure 5C-D showing DNAJ-PKAc and Hsp70 in AKAP-Lbc complexes.

claim: Hsp70 and MEK inhibitor combinations selectively block proliferation of AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
source: Drug screening reveals Hsp70 and MEK inhibitor combinations that selectively block proliferation of AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
evidence: This is supported by drug screening data in Figure 3G-K showing synergistic effects of Ver-155008 (Hsp70 inhibitor) with MEK inhibitors.

claim: DNAJ-PKAc biases the signaling landscape toward ERK activation.
source: Phosphoproteomic profiling demonstrates that DNAJ-PKAc biases the signaling landscape toward ERK activation and engages downstream kinase cascades.
evidence: This is supported by phosphoproteomic data in Figure 6E-F showing 23% of ERK phosphosites were up-regulated in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.

claim: DNAJ-PKAc engages downstream kinase cascades.
source: Phosphoproteomic profiling demonstrates that DNAJ-PKAc biases the signaling landscape toward ERK activation and engages downstream kinase cascades.
evidence: This is supported by phosphoproteomic profiling data showing enrichment of multiple kinase substrates including PKC, DAP kinase, and CDK in Figure 6F.

claim: The oncogenic action of DNAJ-PKAc involves an acquired scaffolding function that permits recruitment of Hsp70.
source: Thus, the oncogenic action of DNAJ-PKAc involves an acquired scaffolding function that permits recruitment of Hsp70 and mobilization of local ERK signaling.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the integration of multiple experimental findings including immunoprecipitation, PLA, and functional studies throughout the manuscript.

claim: The oncogenic action of DNAJ-PKAc involves mobilization of local ERK signaling.
source: Thus, the oncogenic action of DNAJ-PKAc involves an acquired scaffolding function that permits recruitment of Hsp70 and mobilization of local ERK signaling.
evidence: This is supported by data showing elevated basal ERK activation in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells (Figure 5E-I) and heterogeneous ERK activation in FLC tissues (Figure 4B-C).

claim: FLC afflicts healthy adolescents and young adults between the ages of 15–25 with no history of liver disease.
source: This rare cancer afflicts healthy adolescents and young adults between the ages of 15–25 with no history of liver disease.
evidence: This is a well-established clinical characteristic of FLC cited in the introduction.

claim: The overall survival of FLC is 35%.
source: The diagnosis is often made after disease has spread outside the liver, leading to an overall survival of 35% (Ang et al., 2013).
evidence: This statistic is cited from Ang et al., 2013.

claim: FLC frequently recurs.
source: Unfortunately, FLC frequently recurs, as it is intractable to standard chemotherapies and radiation.
evidence: This is a clinical observation about FLC behavior.

claim: FLC is intractable to standard chemotherapies and radiation.
source: Unfortunately, FLC frequently recurs, as it is intractable to standard chemotherapies and radiation.
evidence: This is a well-known clinical characteristic of FLC.

claim: Surgical resection is currently the only opportunity for a cure of FLC.
source: Surgical resection is currently the only opportunity for a cure.
evidence: This reflects current clinical practice for FLC treatment.

claim: The underlying genetic defect in FLC is a heterozygous in-frame deletion of ~400 kb in chromosome 19.
source: Sequencing tumor genomes of FLCs identified the underlying genetic defect as a heterozygous in-frame deletion of ~400 kb in chromosome 19 (Honeyman et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by cited genomic sequencing studies.

claim: The genetic lesion in chromosome 19 leads to translation of a de novo chimeric gene product where the chaperonin-binding domain of heat shock protein 40 (DNAJ) is fused to the Cα subunit of PKA.
source: This genetic lesion leads to translation of a de novo chimeric gene product where the chaperonin-binding domain of heat shock protein 40 (DNAJ) is fused to the Cα subunit of PKA (Cheung et al., 2015; Honeyman et al., 2014) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature and illustrated in Figure 1A showing the structure of DNAJ-PKAc.

claim: DNAJ-PKAc is solely expressed in FLCs.
source: We have recently shown that DNAJ-PKAc is solely expressed in FLCs, is cAMP-responsive, and importantly is incorporated into A-Kinase Anchoring Protein (AKAP) signaling complexes (Riggle et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is supported by the authors' previous work cited as Riggle et al., 2016a.

claim: DNAJ-PKAc is cAMP-responsive.
source: We have recently shown that DNAJ-PKAc is solely expressed in FLCs, is cAMP-responsive, and importantly is incorporated into A-Kinase Anchoring Protein (AKAP) signaling complexes (Riggle et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is supported by the authors' previous work cited as Riggle et al., 2016a.

claim: DNAJ-PKAc is incorporated into A-Kinase Anchoring Protein (AKAP) signaling complexes.
source: We have recently shown that DNAJ-PKAc is solely expressed in FLCs, is cAMP-responsive, and importantly is incorporated into A-Kinase Anchoring Protein (AKAP) signaling complexes (Riggle et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is supported by the authors' previous work and demonstrated in Figure 5C-D.

claim: Human FLCs are heterozygous in that they express both wildtype PKA and the DNAJ-PKAc fusion.
source: Immunoblot screening of clinical samples with antibodies against PKAc revealed that human FLCs are heterozygous in that they express both wildtype PKA and the DNAJ-PKAc fusion (Figure 1B, top panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoblot data in Figure 1B showing both bands corresponding to wildtype PKAc and DNAJ-PKAc.

claim: The type Iα regulatory subunit of PKA (RIα) is elevated in FLC tumors as compared to normal adjacent tissue.
source: Additional biochemical characterization of these clinical samples substantiated the elevated expression of the type Iα regulatory subunit of PKA (RIα) in FLC tumors as compared normal adjacent tissue (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, top panel) (Riggle et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and cited previous work.

claim: Type II regulatory subunit (RII) levels do not fluctuate between FLC and normal tissue.
source: Related experiments demonstrate that type II regulatory subunit (RII) levels do not fluctuate (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, bottom panel).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The active site of DNAJ-PKAc is identical to that of the native kinase.
source: The active site of DNAJ-PKAc is identical to that of the native kinase; both PKA forms are inhibited by PKI and are sensitive to the same spectrum of ATP analog inhibitors (Cheung et al., 2015; Riggle et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is supported by cited biochemical studies.

claim: Both DNAJ-PKAc and native PKA are inhibited by PKI.
source: The active site of DNAJ-PKAc is identical to that of the native kinase; both PKA forms are inhibited by PKI and are sensitive to the same spectrum of ATP analog inhibitors (Cheung et al., 2015; Riggle et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is supported by cited biochemical studies.

claim: Both DNAJ-PKAc and native PKA are sensitive to the same spectrum of ATP analog inhibitors.
source: The active site of DNAJ-PKAc is identical to that of the native kinase; both PKA forms are inhibited by PKI and are sensitive to the same spectrum of ATP analog inhibitors (Cheung et al., 2015; Riggle et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is supported by cited biochemical studies.

claim: Phosphoproteomic profiling of human FLC and adjacent normal liver samples identified 7697 phosphopeptides.
source: Phosphoproteomic profiling of human FLC and adjacent normal liver samples by label-free LC-MS/MS analysis identified 7697 phosphopeptides (Hogrebe et al., 2018) (Figure 1E; n = 6 technical replicates).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 1E.

claim: 628 phosphopeptides were significantly enriched in FLCs as compared to adjacent normal liver.
source: Of these, 628 phosphopeptides were significantly enriched in FLCs as compared to adjacent normal liver (Figure 1E; orange).
evidence: This is shown in the volcano plot in Figure 1E.

claim: Of the phosphosites increased in FLC, 20% were putative PKC targets.
source: Of the phosphosites increased in FLC, 20% were putative PKC targets and 8% were ERK-MAPK sites (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is based on NetworKIN analysis presented in Figure 1F.

claim: Of the phosphosites increased in FLC, 8% were ERK-MAPK sites.
source: Of the phosphosites increased in FLC, 20% were putative PKC targets and 8% were ERK-MAPK sites (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is based on NetworKIN analysis presented in Figure 1F.

claim: PKA phosphosites were only enriched by 6.5% in FLC.
source: Interestingly, PKA phosphosites were only enriched by 6.5%.
evidence: This is derived from the phosphoproteomic analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: DNAJ-PKAc interacts with heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70).
source: Further immunoprecipitation experiments from clinical samples revealed that DNAJ-PKAc interacts with heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70; Figure 1H), a cellular chaperonin that facilitates protein folding and is frequently up-regulated in cancers (Calderwood et al., 2006; Mayer and Bukau, 2005).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 1H.

claim: Hsp70 is a cellular chaperonin that facilitates protein folding.
source: Further immunoprecipitation experiments from clinical samples revealed that DNAJ-PKAc interacts with heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70; Figure 1H), a cellular chaperonin that facilitates protein folding and is frequently up-regulated in cancers (Calderwood et al., 2006; Mayer and Bukau, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Hsp70 function supported by citations.

claim: PLA puncta indicative of native DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 sub-complexes were readily detected in regions of tumor.
source: PLA puncta indicative of native DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 sub-complexes were readily detected in regions of tumor (Figure 1J and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown by PLA imaging data in Figure 1J.

claim: The number of PLA puncta was reduced in adjacent sections of healthy liver compared to tumor.
source: In contrast, the number of PLA puncta was reduced in adjacent sections of healthy liver (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is shown by PLA imaging data in Figure 1I and quantified in Figure 1K.

claim: Recruitment of Hsp70 to DNAJ-PKAc may explain why protein levels of this fusion are frequently elevated compared to native PKA in FLCs.
source: Recruitment of Hsp70 to DNAJ-PKAc may explain why protein levels of this fusion are frequently elevated compared to native PKA in FLCs (Figure 1B, top panel).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observation of elevated DNAJ-PKAc protein levels in Figure 1B and the known role of Hsp70 in protein stabilization.

claim: A 400 kb region was excised between intron 1 of the gene for Hsp40 (Dnajb1) and intron 1 of the gene for PKAc (Prkaca) in AML12 cells.
source: Therefore, we employed CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing of chromosome eight in AML12 non-transformed murine hepatocytes to generate sustainable and homogenous cell lines. A 400 kb region was excised between intron 1 of the gene for Hsp40 (Dnajb1) and intron 1 of the gene for PKAc (Prkaca; Figure 2A).
evidence: This is described in the methods and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: Four gene-edited AML12DNAJ-PKAc cell lines were generated.
source: Quantitative PCR measurement of mRNA transcripts for Dnajb1 and Prkaca in wildtype and four gene-edited AML12DNAJ-PKAc cell lines revealed differential expression of both transcripts in each clonal AML12DNAJ-PKAc cell line (Figure 2C & D, orange).
evidence: This is shown by qPCR data in Figure 2C-E.

claim: These AML12DNAJ-PKAc cell lines encode and express a single copy of DNAJ-PKAc.
source: Characterization by nucleotide sequencing and immunoblot analyses confirmed that these AML12DNAJ-PKAc cell lines encode and express a single copy of DNAJ-PKAc (Figure 2F & G).
evidence: This is confirmed by sequencing data in Figure 2F and immunoblot in Figure 2G.

claim: Introduction of the DNAJ-PKAc allele promotes the up-regulation of RIα expression.
source: As observed in FLCs, introduction of the DNAJ-PKAc allele promote the up-regulation of RIα expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Clone 14 AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells express similar levels of DNAJ-PKAc and native PKA as compared to human FLC patients.
source: Clone 14 was selected for further analyses as these cells express similar levels of DNAJ-PKAc and native PKA as compared to human FLC patients (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot comparison in Figure 2G.

claim: Clonal AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells have similar levels of PKA activity to the wildtype cell line.
source: Interestingly, these clonal AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells have similar levels of PKA activity and comparable migratory properties to the wildtype cell line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–F).
evidence: This is shown by PKA activity assay data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Clonal AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells have comparable migratory properties to the wildtype cell line.
source: Interestingly, these clonal AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells have similar levels of PKA activity and comparable migratory properties to the wildtype cell line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–F).
evidence: This is shown by migration assay data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C-F.

claim: DNAJ-PKAc was detected within Hsp70 immune complexes isolated from AML12DNAJ-PKAc cell line.
source: Immunoblot analysis detected DNAJ-PKAc within Hsp70 immune complexes isolated from our AML12DNAJ-PKAc cell line, while PKAc was not present in Hsp70 immune complexes isolated from control AML12 cells (Figure 2H, top panel).
evidence: This is shown by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 2H.

claim: PKAc was not present in Hsp70 immune complexes isolated from control AML12 cells.
source: Immunoblot analysis detected DNAJ-PKAc within Hsp70 immune complexes isolated from our AML12DNAJ-PKAc cell line, while PKAc was not present in Hsp70 immune complexes isolated from control AML12 cells (Figure 2H, top panel).
evidence: This is shown by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 2H.

claim: AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells have increased amounts of DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 sub-complexes compared to control cells.
source: In contrast, quantitation of PLA puncta (yellow) from >200 AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells revealed increased amounts of the DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 sub-complexes in our gene-edited cell lines (Figure 2J & K).
evidence: This is shown by PLA quantification in Figure 2K.

claim: AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells proliferate more rapidly than wildtype AML12 cells.
source: First, cell proliferation was measured over 72 hr in culture using the MTS assay. Amalgamated data show that AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells proliferate more rapidly than wildtype AML12 cells (Figure 3A; n = 3).
evidence: This is shown by MTS assay data in Figure 3A.

claim: DNA synthesis is increased in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells as compared to wildtype AML12 cells (82 ± 2% vs 36 ± 5%).
source: Second, immunostaining for BrdU incorporation showed that DNA synthesis is increased AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells as compared to wildtype AML12 cells (82 ± 2% vs 36 ± 5%, Figure 3B & C; n = 3).
evidence: This is shown by BrdU incorporation data in Figure 3B-C.

claim: AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells have increased proliferative capacity as compared to wildtype counterparts in colony formation assays.
source: Third, colony formation assays were performed to reinforce our data that AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells have increased proliferative capacity as compared to their wildtype counterparts (Figure 3D; n = 3).
evidence: This is shown by colony formation data in Figure 3D-E.

claim: Ver-155008 is an ATP-analog inhibitor of Hsp70 (IC50 = 0.5 μM).
source: Ver-155008 is an ATP-analog inhibitor of Hsp70 (IC50 = 0.5 μM) that halts cell proliferation in several cancer models (Eugênio et al., 2017; Wen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Ver-155008 halts cell proliferation in several cancer models.
source: Ver-155008 is an ATP-analog inhibitor of Hsp70 (IC50 = 0.5 μM) that halts cell proliferation in several cancer models (Eugênio et al., 2017; Wen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Sole application of Ver-155008 over a range of concentrations did not have a differential effect on the viability of AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells compared to wildtype AML12 cells.
source: However, sole application of this drug over a range of concentrations did not have a differential effect on the viability of AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells compared to wildtype AML12 cells as assessed by MTS assay at 72 hr (Figure 3F; n = 3).
evidence: This is shown by dose-response data in Figure 3F.

claim: Three Hsp70 inhibitor/drug combinations were appreciably more toxic to cells harboring DNAJ-PKAc than to cells only expressing wildtype kinase.
source: Three Hsp70 inhibitor/drug combinations were appreciably more toxic to cells harboring DNAJ-PKAc than to cells only expressing wildtype kinase (Figure 3G–I, pink dots).
evidence: This is shown by drug screening data in Figure 3G-I.

claim: The three compounds identified in the screen were the MEK kinase inhibitors cobimetinib, binimetinib and trametinib.
source: Deconvolution of our screening data revealed that these compounds were the MEK kinase inhibitors cobimetinib, binimetinib and trametinib.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the drug screening data.

claim: Wildtype AML12 cells are sensitive to cobimetinib alone.
source: Dose response curves revealed that wildtype AML12 cells are sensitive to cobimetinib alone (Figure 3J) whereas AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells were more resistant to this drug over the same concentration range (Figure 3K).
evidence: This is shown by dose-response data in Figure 3J.

claim: AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells were more resistant to cobimetinib than wildtype cells over the same concentration range.
source: Dose response curves revealed that wildtype AML12 cells are sensitive to cobimetinib alone (Figure 3J) whereas AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells were more resistant to this drug over the same concentration range (Figure 3K).
evidence: This is shown by dose-response data in Figure 3K.

claim: In the presence of Ver-155008 the cytotoxic effect of cobimetinib in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells was enhanced.
source: Importantly, in the presence of Ver-155008 the cytotoxic effect of cobimetinib in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells was enhanced (Figure 3K).
evidence: This is shown by dose-response data in Figure 3K.

claim: Immunoblot analyses of tumor lysates detect a slight reduction in global phospho-ERK signal in patient samples.
source: Immunoblot analyses of tumor lysates detect a slight reduction in global phospho-ERK signal in patient samples (Figure 4A, top panel).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot data in Figure 4A.

claim: Immunofluorescent staining of tumor sections reveals clusters of prominent phospho-ERK signal in the cancerous hepatocytes.
source: Yet immunofluorescent staining of tumor sections reveals clusters of prominent phospho-ERK signal in the cancerous hepatocytes (Figure 4B & C, yellow; from patient 3).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence imaging in Figure 4B-C.

claim: Regional detection of phospho-ERK is consistent with heterogeneous activation of the ERK cascade within the tumor.
source: Such regional detection of phospho-ERK is consistent with heterogeneous activation of the ERK cascade within the tumor.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the immunofluorescence data in Figure 4B-C.

claim: The phosphoproteomic screen identifies numerous ERK substrates that are elevated in FLC tumor as compared to normal liver.
source: Likewise, the phosphoproteomic screen presented in Figure 1E & F identifies numerous ERK substrates that are elevated in FLC tumor as compared to normal liver (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is shown in the table in Figure 4D listing ERK substrates.

claim: The protein kinase P90RSK is a well-characterized downstream target of ERK.
source: This includes the protein kinase P90RSK, a well-characterized downstream target of ERK (Dalby et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Dalby et al., 1998.

claim: Immunoblot detection of pSer 221-P90RSK indicates variable activation of this kinase in FLC samples.
source: Validation of this ERK phosphorylation event is provided in two ways. First, immunoblot detection of pSer 221-P90RSK indicates variable activation of this kinase in the same cohort of FLC samples (Figure 4E, top panel).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot data in Figure 4E.

claim: Immunofluorescent detection of phospho-P90RSK in tissue sections of FLC uncovered clusters of cells containing activated kinase.
source: Second, immunofluorescent detection of phospho-P90RSK in tissue sections of FLC uncovered clusters of cells containing activated kinase (Figure 4F & G, magenta; from patient 3).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence imaging in Figure 4F-G.

claim: The RAF-MEK-ERK kinase cascade is active in a subset of cells within the heterogeneous intratumoral environment of FLCs.
source: Collectively these findings infer that the RAF-MEK-ERK kinase cascade is active in a subset of cells within the heterogeneous intratumoral environment of FLCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ERK and P90RSK activation data in Figure 4.

claim: AKAP-Lbc is a multifunctional anchoring protein and enhancer of ERK signaling.
source: A logical candidate was AKAP-Lbc, a multifunctional anchoring protein and enhancer of ERK signaling (Smith et al., 2010) that interacts with another scaffolding protein, kinase suppressor of Ras (KSR), to form the core of a signaling network that integrates cAMP regulation of RAF-MEK-ERK signaling (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is cited from Smith et al., 2010.

claim: AKAP-Lbc interacts with kinase suppressor of Ras (KSR) to form the core of a signaling network that integrates cAMP regulation of RAF-MEK-ERK signaling.
source: A logical candidate was AKAP-Lbc, a multifunctional anchoring protein and enhancer of ERK signaling (Smith et al., 2010) that interacts with another scaffolding protein, kinase suppressor of Ras (KSR), to form the core of a signaling network that integrates cAMP regulation of RAF-MEK-ERK signaling (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is established knowledge illustrated in Figure 5A.

claim: AKAP-Lbc protein is up-regulated in human FLCs as compared to normal adjacent liver.
source: We found that AKAP-Lbc protein is up-regulated in human FLCs as compared to normal adjacent liver (Figure 5B, top panel, lane 2) and immunoblot analysis detected DNAJ-PKAc in AKAP-Lbc immune complexes isolated from FLCs (Figure 5C, top panel, lane 2).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot data in Figure 5B.

claim: DNAJ-PKAc is present in AKAP-Lbc immune complexes isolated from FLCs.
source: We found that AKAP-Lbc protein is up-regulated in human FLCs as compared to normal adjacent liver (Figure 5B, top panel, lane 2) and immunoblot analysis detected DNAJ-PKAc in AKAP-Lbc immune complexes isolated from FLCs (Figure 5C, top panel, lane 2).
evidence: This is shown by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 5C.

claim: DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 sub-complexes co-fractionate with AKAP-Lbc in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
source: Parallel experiments show that DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 sub-complexes co-fractionate with this anchoring protein in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells (Figure 5D, top panel, lane 2).
evidence: This is shown by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 5D.

claim: AKAP-Lbc can sequester Hsp70 and DNAJ-PKAc with an ERK signaling module in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells and human FLCs.
source: Thus, AKAP-Lbc can sequester Hsp70 and DNAJ-PKAc with an ERK signaling module in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells and human FLCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 5C-D.

claim: Basal levels of phospho-ERK 1/2 were elevated 2.8 ± 1.5 fold (n = 4) in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells as compared to wildtype controls.
source: Notably, basal levels of phospho-ERK 1/2 were elevated 2.8 ± 1.5 fold (n = 4) in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells as compared to wildtype controls (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot quantification in Figure 5E.

claim: Phospho-ERK signal was barely detectable in control AML12 cells.
source: This finding was confirmed in situ by immunofluorescent detection. Phospho-ERK signal was barely detectable in control AML12 cells (Figure 5F & G), but clearly evident in the cytoplasm of AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells (Figure 5H & I).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence imaging in Figure 5F-G.

claim: Phospho-ERK signal was clearly evident in the cytoplasm of AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
source: This finding was confirmed in situ by immunofluorescent detection. Phospho-ERK signal was barely detectable in control AML12 cells (Figure 5F & G), but clearly evident in the cytoplasm of AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells (Figure 5H & I).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence imaging in Figure 5H-I.

claim: Treatment with Ver-155008 (3 μM) alone had no effect on ERK activation in wildtype cells.
source: In wildtype cells, treatment with Ver-155008 (3 μM) alone had no effect on ERK activation (Figure 5J, top panel, lanes 1 and 2).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot data in Figure 5J.

claim: Administration of cobimetinib (100 nM) abolished detection of the phospho-ERK signal in wildtype cells.
source: However, administration of cobimetinib (100 nM) or a combination of both drugs abolished detection of the phospho-ERK signal (Figure 5J, top panel, lanes 3 and 4).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot data in Figure 5J.

claim: Treatment with Ver-155008 (3 μM) alone had a modest effect on phospho-ERK signal in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
source: In contrast, basal phospho-ERK levels were high in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells, treatment with Ver-155008 (3 μM) alone had a modest effect on phospho-ERK signal (Figure 5J, top panel, lanes 5 and 6).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot data in Figure 5J.

claim: Application of cobimetinib (100 nM) or in combination with Ver-155008 abolished detection of phospho-ERK signals in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
source: Application of cobimetinib (100 nM) or in combination with Ver-155008 abolished detection of phospho-ERK signals (Figure 5J, top panel, lanes 7 and 8).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot data in Figure 5J.

claim: Dual inhibition of Hsp70 and elements of the RAF-MEK-ERK cascade impedes mitogenic signals to preferentially block proliferation of AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
source: Thus, dual inhibition of Hsp70 and elements of the RAF-MEK-ERK cascade impedes mitogenic signals to preferentially block proliferation of AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the drug treatment data in Figure 5J-K.

claim: The synergistic effect of cobimetinib (100 nM) and Ver-155008 (3 μM) blocked AML12DNAJ-PKAc cell proliferation more potently than either drug alone.
source: This postulate was confirmed by clonogenic growth assays that monitor colony formation. Crystal violet staining showed that the synergistic effect of cobimetinib (100 nM) and Ver-155008 (3 μM) blocked AML12DNAJ-PKAc cell proliferation more potently than either drug alone (Figure 5K).
evidence: This is shown by colony formation data in Figure 5K.

claim: Mutation of a conserved HPD motif that demarks a critical loop in the DNAJ domain abolishes interaction with Hsp70.
source: Mutation of a conserved HPD motif that demarks a critical loop in the DNAJ domain abolishes interaction with Hsp70 (Hennessy et al., 2005) (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is cited from Hennessy et al., 2005.

claim: Substitution of H33 to Q in the context of DNAJ-PKAc prevents association with endogenous Hsp70 in AML12 cells.
source: Thus, substitution of H33 to Q in the context of DNAJ-PKAc would be expected to prevent association with endogenous Hsp70 in AML12 cells (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is shown by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 6B.

claim: Introduction of the H33Q mutation greatly reduces the level of Hsp70 in AKAP-Lbc complexes.
source: Introduction of the H33Q mutation greatly reduces the level of Hsp70 in AKAP-Lbc complexes (Figure 6C, top panel, lane 3).
evidence: This is shown by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 6C.

claim: Addition of the J-domain onto the N-terminus of PKAc induces a novel interaction with Hsp70.
source: The simplest explanation of this result is that addition of the J-domain onto the N-terminus of PKAc induces a novel interaction with Hsp70, thereby permitting the recruitment of this chaperonin to AKAP signaling islands.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the immunoprecipitation data in Figure 6C.

claim: Basal levels of phospho-ERK were elevated upon introduction of DNAJ-PKAc in wildtype AML12 cells.
source: Immunoblot detection confirmed that basal levels of phospho-ERK were elevated upon introduction of DNAJ-PKAc in wildtype AML12 cells while transfection with the DNAJ-PKAc H33Q mutant diminished ERK activation (Figure 6D, top panel).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot data in Figure 6D.

claim: Transfection with the DNAJ-PKAc H33Q mutant diminished ERK activation.
source: Immunoblot detection confirmed that basal levels of phospho-ERK were elevated upon introduction of DNAJ-PKAc in wildtype AML12 cells while transfection with the DNAJ-PKAc H33Q mutant diminished ERK activation (Figure 6D, top panel).
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot data in Figure 6D.

claim: Phosphoproteomic profiling identified 2912 unique phosphopeptides in wildtype and AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
source: Independent support for our hypothesis was provided through a phosphoproteomic screen that identified 2912 unique phosphopeptides in wildtype and AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 6E.

claim: 96 phosphopeptides were increased in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
source: Of these, 96 phosphopeptides were increased (orange) and 76 were reduced in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells (black).
evidence: This is shown in the volcano plot in Figure 6E.

claim: 76 phosphopeptides were reduced in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
source: Of these, 96 phosphopeptides were increased (orange) and 76 were reduced in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells (black).
evidence: This is shown in the volcano plot in Figure 6E.

claim: 23% of ERK phosphosites were up-regulated in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
source: Substrate profiling using the NetworKIN platform revealed that 23% of ERK phosphosites were up-regulated in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells whereas only 3% of PKA consensus sites were enriched (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is based on NetworKIN analysis presented in Figure 6F.

claim: Only 3% of PKA consensus sites were enriched in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells.
source: Substrate profiling using the NetworKIN platform revealed that 23% of ERK phosphosites were up-regulated in AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells whereas only 3% of PKA consensus sites were enriched (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is based on NetworKIN analysis presented in Figure 6F.

claim: DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 macromolecular assemblies bias the signaling landscape toward ERK activation and mobilize other downstream kinase networks.
source: This systemwide analysis suggests that DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 macromolecular assemblies bias the signaling landscape toward ERK activation and mobilize other downstream kinase networks.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the phosphoproteomic data in Figure 6E-F.

claim: Formation of DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 sub-complexes in FLC is an example of 'chaperonopathies by mistake'.
source: We believe that formation of DNAJ-PKAc/Hsp70 sub-complexes in FLC is an example of this latter category (Calderwood et al., 2006; Mayer and Bukau, 2005; Whitesell and Lindquist, 2005).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the concept of chaperonopathies and the data showing Hsp70 recruitment to DNAJ-PKAc.

claim: Recruitment of Hsp70 through the DNAJ domain preferentially stabilizes the chimeric PKAc fusion protein.
source: Chaperonins can repair misfolded proteins to reduce cellular stress or, as we believe is the case in FLC, recruitment of Hsp70 through the DNAJ domain preferentially stabilizes the chimeric PKAc fusion protein.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observation of elevated DNAJ-PKAc protein levels and Hsp70 interaction.

claim: Protein levels of the DNAJ-PKAc variant are elevated in tumor samples and disease-relevant cell lines as compared to native PKA.
source: This hypothesis is borne out by data in Figures 1B and 2G wherein we demonstrate that protein levels of the DNAJ-PKAc variant are elevated in tumor samples and disease-relevant cell lines as compared to native PKA.
evidence: This is shown by immunoblot data in Figures 1B and 2G.

claim: The abnormal pairing of Hsp70 with DNAJ-PKAc creates new and unique drug targets.
source: In addition, the abnormal pairing of Hsp70 with DNAJ-PKAc creates new and unique drug targets.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the drug screening results showing synergy between Hsp70 and MEK inhibitors.

claim: Whole exome sequencing confirms that FLCs lack activating mutations in Ras or B-RAF.
source: First, whole exome sequencing confirms that FLCs lack activating mutations in Ras or B-RAF, but rather arise from a monogenic lesion in chromosome 19 that produces the DNAJ-PKAc fusion (Cornella et al., 2015; Lalazar and Simon, 2018; Simon et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from multiple genomic sequencing studies.

claim: FLCs arise from a monogenic lesion in chromosome 19 that produces the DNAJ-PKAc fusion.
source: First, whole exome sequencing confirms that FLCs lack activating mutations in Ras or B-RAF, but rather arise from a monogenic lesion in chromosome 19 that produces the DNAJ-PKAc fusion (Cornella et al., 2015; Lalazar and Simon, 2018; Simon et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from multiple genomic sequencing studies.

claim: Drugs targeting upstream elements of the ERK cascade (EGF receptor antagonists and B-RAF inhibitors) were ineffective or exhibited modest antiproliferative effects when used in combination with Ver-155008.
source: Second, our screen of FDA approved anti-cancer compounds in Figure 3H and I reveals that drugs targeting upstream elements of the ERK cascade, including EGF receptor antagonists erlotinib, lapatinib and afatinib and the B-RAF inhibitors dabrafenib and vemurafenib were ineffective, or at best exhibited modest antiproliferative effects when used in combination with Ver-155008.
evidence: This is based on the drug screening data in Figure 3H-I.

claim: The ERK inhibitor GDC-0994 had little effect on proliferation in combination screens with Ver-155008.
source: Interestingly, the ERK inhibitor GDC-0994 had little effect on proliferation in these combination screens.
evidence: This is based on the drug screening data.

claim: The exquisite sensitivity of AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells to MEK inhibition suggests that DNAJ-PKAc may be acting downstream of Ras-Raf activation.
source: Therefore, we interpret the exquisite sensitivity of AML12DNAJ-PKAc cells to MEK inhibition to suggest that DNAJ-PKAc may be acting downstream of Ras-Raf activation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the drug screening data showing selective sensitivity to MEK inhibitors.

claim: Anchored PKA activity has been implicated in the phosphorylation of RAF kinase and KSR-1 in the context of AKAP-Lbc signaling complexes.
source: Anchored PKA activity has been implicated in the phosphorylation of RAF kinase and KSR-1 in the context of AKAP-Lbc signaling complexes (Smith et al., 2017; Smith et al., 2010; Takahashi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The phosphoproteomic analysis identifies elevated PKA phosphorylation of serine 838 on KSR in FLCs.
source: In keeping with this molecular mechanism, our phosphoproteomic analysis identifies elevated PKA phosphorylation of serine 838 on KSR in FLCs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown in the table in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Hsp90 and certain Hsp70 isoforms are elements of KSR scaffolds.
source: This is especially interesting in light of early findings that Hsp90 and certain Hsp70 isoforms are elements of KSR scaffolds (Stewart et al., 1999) and data in Figure 5B–D showing that the chaperonins including the Hsp70-DNAJ-PKAc subcomplex are selectively recruited to AKAP-Lbc-KSR signaling units in FLC.
evidence: This is cited from Stewart et al., 1999.

claim: Each MEK inhibitor identified in the screen has been approved for the treatment of melanoma and other cancers.
source: Accordingly, each MEK inhibitor identified in our screen has been approved for the treatment of melanoma and other cancers (Caunt et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from Caunt et al., 2015.

claim: Clinical trials with Hsp70 inhibitors hold promise for the treatment of cancers.
source: This could be an important consideration for Ver-155008 as clinical trials with other Hsp70 inhibitors hold promise for the treatment of cancers (Goloudina et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from Goloudina et al., 2012.

claim: FLC has distinctive histologic features.
source: Fibrolamellar carcinoma (FLC) is a variant of liver cancer that has distinctive histologic features (Craig et al., 1980).
evidence: This is cited from Craig et al., 1980.

claim: Intratumoral heterogeneity is distinct from the undulating sinusoidal pattern of normal liver.
source: This 'intratumoral heterogeneity' is distinct from the undulating sinusoidal pattern of normal liver (Figure 1C & D).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence imaging comparing normal liver and FLC in Figure 1C-D.

claim: Abolishing the binding of Hsp70 to DNAJ-PKAc complex decreases ERK signaling.
source: Indirect support for this notion is presented in Figure 6D showing that abolishing the binding of Hsp70 to DNAJ-PKAc complex decreases ERK signaling.
evidence: This is shown by the H33Q mutant data in Figure 6D.

claim: The preferential stabilization of DNAJ-PKAc proceeds through the local action of Hsp70.
source: Thus, we postulate that the preferential stabilization of DNAJ-PKAc proceeds through the local action of Hsp70.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the Hsp70 interaction data and elevated DNAJ-PKAc protein levels.

claim: Recruitment of Hsp70 via the DNAJ domain in the chimeric DNAJ-PKAc kinase is an important new element that contributes to the dysregulation of this unique fusion enzyme.
source: Rather, we propose that recruitment of Hsp70 via the DNAJ domain in the chimeric DNAJ-PKAc kinase is an important new element that contributes to the dysregulation of this unique fusion enzyme.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript based on all the experimental data.
